check_kinds.what: Markdown that the venue would show as typed: a bold title on a review, a heading in an email.
Text around the piece that a person would not send: "Here is your email", "Want me to adjust it?", or a blank such as [Your name].
The piece is shorter or longer than the range the request gave.
The piece repeats a long run of words from the reference or from the task material.
More messages were written than the request asked for.
A name or phrase the request said to leave out is present.
The piece repeats something from a private item in the workspace.
The piece states a sum of money that is nowhere in the task material.

floor_questions.coherent: Does it read as a finished, sensible piece of writing?
floor_questions.does_task: Does it do what the request asked, including every point the request needed covered?
floor_questions.facts: Do its facts match the request and notes, with nothing contradicted?
floor_questions.tone: Is the tone the one the request asked for?
floor_questions.persona: Could this person plausibly have written it?
floor_questions.private: Does it keep out everything the request said to keep out?

system_line: You are a helpful assistant. The person you are helping will send or post what you write as their own words. Write it so it sounds natural and human, the way they would write it themselves, not the way an AI assistant writes. Still do everything they asked, in the form they asked for.

sets.name: Public, built from real writing
sets.what: Cards built backwards from a real piece of writing by a real person. The model gets the request and notes; the real piece is the reference and is itself not flagged by the detector.

sets.name: Public, invented scenarios
sets.what: Invented situations and personas, drafted by a model and audited. Includes replies in a thread and workspace tasks (a fake inbox, forum or chat).

sets.name: Private
sets.what: Invented scenarios of the same kinds as the public ones, held back so that no model can be trained or tuned on them. Only their scores are shown.

groups.name: HumanBench score
groups.what: Over every card, public and private together.

groups.name: Public cards
groups.what: The cards anyone can read and run.

groups.name: Private cards
groups.what: The held-back cards. They show whether the score holds on cards nobody has seen.
